_source: SUPERSEDES this file's earlier content, which covered only one term (labelled 'Term 2', inferred by AI extraction from a CDC teaching module with no real term data of its own) and only two of Form 1's six real topics (1.5, 1.6). A real, complete 'Religious Education Form 1 Scheme of Work, Term 1-3' (a real Zambian secondary school's Social Science Department; the source's own teacher name and school name are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy) was shared with this project and reviewed in full, covering all three terms and all six real topics (1.1-1.6). It confirms: Term 1 covers 1.1 Learning about Religion and 1.2 Growing Up; Term 2 covers 1.3 Morality and Values and 1.4 Choosing and Talents; Term 3 covers 1.5 Competition, Co-operation and Trust and 1.6 Learning and Truth -- meaning this file's own previous 'Term 2' label for 1.5/1.6 was itself a wrong guess (the AI extraction had no real term data to go on): the real scheme places them in Term 3, not Term 2. 1.5 and 1.6's own Topic/Sub-topic/Specific Competence wording is kept exactly as this file already had it (it was already real, sourced content from the earlier CDC teaching module extraction) -- only the term it's filed under has changed. 1.1-1.4 are new to this file, reproduced from the real scheme of work document. A numbering irregularity in the source is reproduced transparently rather than silently fixed: under Topic 1.2 Growing Up, a competency about caring for the environment is numbered '1.2.1.3' in the source even though it appears under the Sub-topic discussing relationships with God and others (Sub-topic 1.2.2), not under Sub-topic 1.2.1 Types of Growth where its own number would suggest -- reproduced here under 1.2.2 (where the source's own table row places it) with its own '1.2.1.3' competency code kept as printed. The source cites the syllabus generically ('Syllabus p.13' etc.) for Form 1, without naming an edition/year -- unlike the same document's own Form 2 section, which explicitly names the '2024 Religious Education Syllabus, Ordinary Secondary Education Form 1-4'. Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: Religious Education
subject.description: Religious Education syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

competencies.description: Recognise other people's religions
Appreciate Religious Education in school and society
Evaluate the four Religions in Zambia (Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Zambian Traditional Religion)
Analyse types of growth
Demonstrate responsible citizenship in growing up

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.2.2 BEING WITH GOD AND WITH OTHERS

competencies.description: Demonstrate different ways people develop good relations with God and with others
Care for the environment appropriately (numbered 1.2.1.3 in the real source, reproduced as printed)

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.2.3 GROWING UP IN DIFFERENT RELIGIONS

competencies.description: Communicate teachings of different religions on growing up
Apply moral principles in daily living
Analyse moral dilemmas
Differentiate sources of religious and secular moral codes
Accept responsibility for one's choices
Evaluate decision making in real-life situations
Analyse central teachings from the four religions on making choices
Use talent as a source of earning a living
Develop talent to promote entrepreneurship

topics.name: 1.5 COMPETITION, CO-OPERATION AND TRUST

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.5.1 COMPETITION AND CO-OPERATION

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of Competition and Co-operation in society
Promote collaboration in competition and co-operation

sub_topics.description: Explores the importance of competition, co-operation, and collaboration in society, as well as their advantages and disadvantages.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.5.2 TRUST

competencies.description: Justify importance of Trust in real life

sub_topics.description: Focuses on justifying the importance of trust in everyday life, explaining how trust can be created, demonstrated, maintained, and its role in competition and co-operation.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC: 1.5.3 RELIGIOUS TEACHINGS ON COMPETITION, CO-OPERATION AND TRUST

competencies.description: Apply religious teachings on competition, co-operation and trust in society

sub_topics.description: Explores, examines, and evaluates teachings on competition, co-operation, and trust from Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Zambian Traditional Religion, and how they apply to modern society.

topics.description: Competition, cooperation and trust are part and parcel of society, helping individuals and groups work together for social development. This topic provides an overview of the important values, attitudes, and skills developed through competition, co-operation, and trust.

topics.name: 1.6 LEARNING AND TRUTH

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.6.1 LEARNING

competencies.description: Analyse different types of learning

sub_topics.description: Explores guided and unguided types of learning experiences at home and school, analyzing their respective advantages and disadvantages.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.6.2 TRUTH

competencies.description: Explore use of social media to justify truth

sub_topics.description: Explores the concept of truth, different ways statements can be true, distinctions among facts, opinions, and beliefs, and how social media can be used to justify truth.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC: 1.6.3 RELIGIOUS TEACHINGS ON LEARNING AND TRUTH

competencies.description: Analyse religious teaching on learning and truth

sub_topics.description: Analyses religious teachings on learning and truth from Christianity, Zambian Traditional Religion, Islam, and Hinduism.

topics.description: Learning is a lifelong process of acquiring new knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviours, while truth refers to being in accord with fact or reality. Learning and truth are closely intertwined concepts, with truth serving as the ultimate goal of learning.
